note: Mean resultant acceleration is approximately 9.8-10 m/s^2 across exercises. This strongly suggests the static gravitational component remains present. Retain the feature for reproducibility, but do not describe it as pure dynamic movement intensity. Interpret absolute changes cautiously.
Variability of resultant acceleration is less dominated by the constant gravitational component and is therefore a more direct descriptor of changes in dynamic wrist motion.

A large absolute dz can occur even when the absolute or percentage change is small if within-trajectory changes are highly consistent. Effect size must therefore be interpreted with change magnitude and directional consistency.

Large changes in pose range require comparison with segment duration and labelled repetition count before biomechanical interpretation, because segment composition may influence range-based summaries.
Heart rate remains excluded from Script 03 movement figures and is retained as a separate physiological analysis.
